# Decision register

The single list of decisions later work may rely on. It has one row per decision, taken from:
- the gate documents and RFCs of the first roadmap;
- the decision sections of the suite documents;
- the binding decisions both roadmaps carry forward.

A verdict a document states but this register does not list is evidence, not permission.

**The count at creation (2026-09-29):** 82 rows.
- **RATIFIED:** 78.
  - 4 reviewed by Carl;
  - 74 ratified by delegation under his standing instruction of 2026-09-29, which is not a review of the verdict.
- **PROPOSED:** 4.
- **DELEGATED, SUPERSEDED, REVERSED:** none.

Every row ratified by delegation is on Carl's ratification docket, which sits outside the repository beside the roadmaps. Each stays his to review, revise or reverse.

## How to use this register

- **Statuses.** A row has one of five:
  - **RATIFIED**: Carl has confirmed it, directly or by the delegation his standing instruction of 2026-09-29 gives. The row says which, when and where.
  - **DELEGATED**: decided on a recommendation while Carl was away, and not yet ratified in either way.
  - **SUPERSEDED**: replaced by a later decision, which the row names.
  - **REVERSED**: withdrawn. The row says by whom, when and why.
  - **PROPOSED**: a decision Roadmap II introduces, adopted when the prompts it names land.
- **Building on a row:**
  - a prompt may build on a **RATIFIED** row;
  - it may build on a **DELEGATED** row only if its Run condition says so, and it records the dependency in its PR;
  - it may never build on a **REVERSED** row.
- **Changing a status:** Carl edits the row, in a one-line commit that says why. A delegated ratification he reviews becomes "Reviewed by Carl, <date>" in the fifth column; a verdict he rejects becomes **REVERSED**, with the reason.
- **Adding decisions:** a new gate adds its rows when its decision document lands. tests/decisionRegister.test.js fails if any `*_GATE.md` or `*_RFC.md` has no row.
- **The Roadmap II prompts column** names the prompts that rely on the row, as the roadmap's run conditions do.

Angles are dimensionless but carried as angles, a magnitude scales only by a plain number, a unit not stated is refused, and a result has a registry unit, is dimensionless or says it has none. Uncertainty is first order for uncorrelated inputs through partial derivatives (a quantity used twice is differentiated once); an input with none gives a result with none, an interval is refused with a pointer to the bootstrap, and an aggregate sharing an input is not propagated. Arguments separate with `;` (and `,` in English) so Spanish decimals read through the shared reader. The module's own ceiling is 6,144 bytes gzipped for the language (measured 5,808) and 6,656 for the language with the question grader (measured 6,228), held by `tests/formula.test.js`. | **RATIFIED** | Recommended and taken on Carl's instruction to go with the recommendation, 2026-10-11; not yet reviewed; reviewed by Carl: ratified directly in chat on 2026-10-13 (all delegated rows) | Carl rejecting the grammar or asking for a different uncertainty rule | 100 |

It is a module of its own, imported only by lazy chunks (the Observatory's panels), so no sources-route request moved (figure 117 of 117, Studio 40 of 40, composer 29, Observatory 16) and no size ceiling moved; deferred 2033.1 of 2033.2 KB. Rule (cheap, in the architecture check): a module that exports `mount*` and calls `addEventListener` without importing the helper is reported unless it is in `tools/listener-helper-allowlist.json`; the record may only shrink (a module that adopts the helper must leave it). Every module-size ceiling is exact, so adopting the helper costs a module its few lines (an import, a scope, an `off()`): the fit panel took it line-neutral (one-line `destroy`), the other fifteen mounting modules are recorded and take it in the slice that makes room, which is why no ceiling was raised. Scopes live as long as their mount: a registration made on something a panel redraws (rows, parameter fields) stays a plain `addEventListener`, because a scope holds what it was given until `off()` and would keep every discarded control alive. The Composer and the Studio are single pages that wire once and rebuild their editors on elements the rebuild discards; neither mounts and unmounts a panel, so neither takes the helper, and the census proves twenty rebuilds of each add no listener. LEAK FOUND AND FIXED (5f20a3b4): the Observatory's fit panel put a `change` listener on its host (`#obsFitBody`) when mounted and never took it back; every language change re-mounts the panel at the same host, so each one left another, all running price() on every change in the fit form (40 across twenty cycles of two changes). `destroy()` now calls `off()`. Regression test: `e2e/lessonPerformance.spec.js` (Observatory cycle with a language change; 40 growth before the fix, 0 after; allowance 4). No other leak: the census on the Observatory's six panels, the Composer and the Studio shows 0 growth over twenty cycles once the fit panel is fixed. The census learned that a listener added with a signal is gone when the signal aborts. | **RATIFIED** | Decided on the recommendation under Carl's standing instruction, 2026-10-12; pending Carl's ratification; reviewed by Carl: ratified directly in chat on 2026-10-13 (all delegated rows) | Adopting the helper in all sixteen mounting modules now (raises sixteen exact ceilings); putting the helper in an existing module (every module's ceiling is exact and the pages share no module with the Observatory); a scope per panel for redrawn controls (retains them) | 107 |

| D-CANMOVE-01 | The grace period of `BlackHole.can_move` is 50 simulated units, the old 10 wall-clock seconds at 1x speed, counted in integrated simulated time (D-R7-03) | `js/physics.js` (e883a004) | decision: a hole made while the world is Static (a merger or collapse product, a hole the user places) moves until 50 units of simulated time have been integrated since it was made, then holds still; an Orbiting world always moves. 50 is 10 s times 5 units per second, which is `frameAdvance` at sim_speed 1 (50 * DT, DT = 0.1): what the wall-clock window came to on a machine drawing 20 frames a second or more at the sandbox's own speed. Why this length: it keeps the sandbox, where holes are placed at 1x, as it was, and it is a fixed length of simulated time, not scaled by playback speed, because the engine does not know the playback speed and must not (the answer would then depend on a control, not on the model). Consequences, stated: (1) the window no longer runs while the simulation is paused, so a hole placed during a pause moves for its 50 units once play resumes, where the wall clock had often used the window up; (2) a world that plays at a high sim_speed (scenarios with sim_speed in the hundreds) crosses 50 units in a fraction of a second of play, so a new hole there freezes almost at once, where it had drifted for 10 real seconds; (3) a backward step gives the window back, so a reversed run retraces the forward one. The window is counted per hole in the steps taken (a non-enumerable `graceUsed`, advanced where the hole's step is applied), not stamped on the clock: a restore builds every hole as new and then sets the clock to the saved one (`js/world.js` `applyShareState`), and a stamp would have been measured from the clock as it was before that write, stretching or erasing the window when the saved clock was earlier or later, or after `resetSimulationTime`. `tests/blackHoleCanMoveRestore.test.js` holds those three cases. Not changed: `creationTime` stays on the hole as a wall-clock stamp nothing reads, and `movementGracePeriod` stays 10 (seconds of play at 1x), so the serialized hole in the scenario goldens is byte-identical; `graceUsed` is not an own enumerable key for the same reason. Removing the dead stamp and storing the window in simulated units is a follow-up that moves `tests/fixtures/scenarioGeometryGolden.json` (7 rows) and 13 hashes in `tests/scenarioGeometry.test.js`, and is Carl's to approve. Evidence: `tests/blackHoleCanMove.test.js` drives one world on a 60 fps and a 15 fps machine: before, at 45 simulated units the 60 fps hole could move (9.0 s) and the 15 fps one could not (12.0 s), having stopped at x = 37.25 against 45; after, both can move at 45, both are static at 70, and they stop within one frame's advance of each other. | **RATIFIED** | Decided on the recommendation under Carl's ratification of D-R7-03 (2026-10-14, "Go with your recommendation on all"); the chosen length is the implementer's, pending Carl's review; reviewed by Carl: ratified directly in chat on 2026-10-15 (all decisions then waiting on him; "For each of those decisions that your are waiting for me on,  go with your best recommendation as my decision"; the recommendation is the decision) | Carl choosing a length scaled by playback speed (the engine would need sim_speed), or keeping the wall-clock window. | 113  |

Seeded stepping exists (a caller may run `withSeed` around stepping, as the new `tools/seeded-step.mjs` does), particles and ripples feed nothing back, but the builders' draws shift the stream that the collision and fragment code draws from (about `updatePhysics`'s black hole and gas giant merging and `handle_rocky_collisions`): without the module, stellar-graveyard diverged on all ten seeds (largest relative difference 1.47 on seed 9), galactic-collision on all ten, compact-object-zoo on four of ten, and debris counts differed (71 against 65). The review that found it showed that with the builders kept and only particle creation stubbed there are no differences. So the builders stay in `js/physics.js` (verbatim, comments trimmed as before): the stream is then the same in every realm by construction, not by import discipline, and a new Worker or script that never imports `js/bodyEffects.js` cannot fork it. The empty pool hands back a scratch particle because the builders set glow fields on the returned particle behind `if (particle)`, and one of those assignments draws (`glow_intensity`); a null would skip that draw. What the effects-less engine does differently is only that no particle exists and nothing is drawn; the ripples the builders push are made in every realm. The thirteen bursts (a black hole absorbing a body, a disk tracer falling in, a star merger, a star swallowing a planet, a gas giant or an asteroid, a rocky collision, the three collapses, a gas giant's impact plume, a gas giant merger and its ignition) were thirteen loops of about twenty lines. They are now `BURSTS` (count, speed and lifetime) and `burst(name, pos, color, aim)` in `js/physics.js`: per particle one draw for the direction, one for the speed, then one for the lifetime, in the old order and with the old expressions (`Math.random() * range + floor`); a plume draws its direction around an aim, and a null color draws the first two and spawns nothing, which is what the absorption burst always did when a body's color was not a hex string (the color is worked out once before the loop, no draw depends on it). Count, speed and lifetime are random draws, so by D-DECOMP-16 they cannot leave the engine; what a burst looks like can. `burstLooks` (start size, end size, color of each burst) and `tracerColor(o)` (was `AccretionDiskParticle.getTemperatureColor`, 33 lines, read by its drawer and by the engine's own absorption burst) are in `js/bodyEffects.js` and filed with the engine by `registerEffects({ pool, looks, tracer })`, in the same module as the pool, so any realm with a pool has the colors and a realm without one has an empty look that nothing reads. `js/physics.js` 6,763 to 6,594 lines (ceiling lowered with `--record-sizes`), and the module ceilings are all exact so nothing could grow: `js/bodyEffects.js` took the 70 added lines by trimming the double-tap recognizer's history and per-method comments (343 to 341, ceiling lowered by 2), `js/bodyDrawSky.js` changed one import line, and no ceiling rose. NOT MOVED, with reasons. (1) The four explosion builders and their palettes: their sizes, lifetimes, glow and the color index are draws interleaved with the data, and the palette length is part of the index draw; a table would need the engine to hold each palette's length, which was judged more coupling than 26 lines of data were worth under a module ceiling that cannot take them. (2) The absorption burst's color gate: whether a body's base color is a hex string decides whether the lifetime is drawn, so that test stays beside the draws. (3) The gas giant's ring state (D-DECOMP-15, state). (4) The display glue (`DRAW_MIN_RADIUS_PX`, `liveBodyCount`, the four-radii note, about 30 lines): re-pointing `js/render.js` at `js/bodyVisuals.js` costs it four lines under an exact ceiling, for six lines out of the engine; left. (5) View code and picking (about 190 lines): `js/ui.js`, which this slice may not edit, imports `screen_to_world`, `findObjectAtPosition`, `resetTrailTick` and `SPACE_OBJECT_NAMES` from the engine, and the engine must not import the render layer to re-export them; `is_offscreen` is not appearance at all, it culls bodies off the canvas inside `updatePhysics` (11 call sites), so the engine's result depends on the page's canvas size and camera zoom (a zero-size canvas, which a Worker has, culls nothing). They move after the `js/ui.js` decomposition closes or through Part B's viewport seam. (6) Trails (the reference frame reads them) and names (`getRandomName` draws) stay. Seeded realm test (`tests/effectsRealm.test.js`) unchanged and green. PART B, design of the engine/ split (no code). AUDIT. `js/physics.js` has 6,594 lines, about 120 exports, 49 importers in `js/` (50 test files, 53 e2e specs, 20 tools; two Worker bundles carry the whole engine, the experiment runner and the validation Worker; the Barnes-Hut worker carries none), and 67 mutable module bindings: 62 `let` (14 body lists that `updatePhysics` and the mergers REASSIGN about 30 times, so importers hold live bindings and a test that captures one clears a detached copy; the settings object, replaced by a spread in `updatePhysicsSettings`; the camera/frame reference, the clocks and counters (`simulationTime`, `PhysicsObject_id_counter`, `worldGeneration`, `interventionEpoch`), `detailScale`, `trailTick`, `liveBodyCount`; seven Barnes-Hut worker variables; seven conservation and absorption accounting variables; fourteen integrator scratch Float64Arrays; six gravity cache variables; the collision grid; the pool, looks and tracer registrations) and 5 mutable containers (the drawers table, the step listeners, the barycenter cache, the grid buckets, the energy history). Sixteen exports have no importer in any source, test, spec or tool (the energy functions, `getAllPhysicsObjects`, two radius constants, `gwaves`, `handle_star_object_collisions` and others) and can be unexported in the slice that moves their code. What is not pure or Worker-safe today: `canvas` and `is_offscreen` (culling by the page's canvas and zoom, 11 sites), three `window` event dispatches (`dispatchSimulationEvent`, `gravitasMerge`, `gravitasWorkerFailed`) already behind `typeof` guards, wall-clock reads that reach the result (`BlackHole.can_move` compares `Date.now()` with the hole's creation time for a ten second grace period, so a newly made static hole moves for ten real seconds, which is a real nondeterminism that a headless fast-forward does not share; the ripples' `time` and `created` stamps feed only the renderer) and the Worker client. REGIONS (lines now): constants and units 140, state and settings and registries 500, events 40, conservation and absorption accounting 420 (accounting 100), energy history 470, force sources and caches 400, integrators 355, `updatePhysics` 740 (of which the Barnes-Hut worker dispatch is 150), the classes 1,575 (black hole and tracer 575, picking 140), collision grid 180, explosion builders and bursts 330, mergers and collapse and accretion 780, exports 130. PROPOSED SLICES, each behind `js/physics.js` kept as the one facade that re-exports (`export { x } from` keeps live bindings), so no importer and nothing in `js/ui.js` changes until the last slice: S1 `state` (the 14 lists with setters replacing the 30 reassignments, the settings and their update, the clocks and counters, the camera reference, the registries; about 330 lines; risk: a reassignment site missed, or an importer's live binding detached; proved by `e2e/worldConstruction.spec.js`, the world golden, `tests/update-physics.test.js`, a new facade test that pins the export list and that an importer's `planets` is the engine's after a step, `validate:physics` identical, `tools/seeded-step.mjs`); S2 `events` (the dispatches behind one sink the page registers, a Worker leaves empty; 90 lines; `tests/effectsRealm.test.js`, the merger e2e, the `gravitasMerge` listeners in the e2e specs); S3 `conservation` and `energy` (read-only over S1; 900 lines; the conservation tests, `validate:physics` conservation checks, the energy tab e2e); S4 `forces` and `integrator` (755 lines, the numerically sensitive pair, moved verbatim; `validate:physics` 304 of 304 identical, gravity assist, binary planets, black hole e2e, and `npm run perf` because a call now crosses a module); S5 `bodies` (classes without the black hole, two files under 1,500; `kind` accessor, saved states, `e2e/scenarioContract.spec.js`, `bodyPlacement`) and `blackHole` (black hole, tracer, absorption); S6 `collisions` (grid, rocky, gas giants, bursts) and `mergers` (the four builders, star merging, collapse): the RNG-order slices, proved by `effects-trace`, `effectsMissing`, `effectsRealm` and the 304; S7 `step` (`updatePhysics`) and `host` (the Barnes-Hut worker client, `clearCachedGravity`, the sink) with the viewport seam: a `setViewport(fn)` the page registers with the current culling rule, so a Worker, which registers nothing, culls nothing exactly as its zero-size canvas does today; proved by the Barnes-Hut e2e, the dist suite and the Worker bundles. Then a rule in `check:architecture` that the engine folder names no `document`, `window`, `localStorage` or `CustomEvent`, and the facade's importers migrate with the next feature that touches them. THE FIRST SLICE SHOULD BE S1, because every other piece reads the settings, the lists or the clocks and cannot leave `js/physics.js` without a cycle until they have a home; it is mechanical, it moves no number, and it is the seam the one-settings-truth work (step 2c, D-DECOMP-14) and any future multi-world need. RISKS. (a) Requests: the sources routes load one file per module and sit on their request ceilings (figure 117 of 117), so about ten new files are ten requests on every route that loads the engine; the standing rule that no request ceiling rises means either a fold of one-importer modules per slice (few remain on the figure route) or a decision by Carl before S2 on how the sources routes count an engine folder (the shipped build bundles it, and its request counts were unchanged by the earlier slices). (b) The bundler groups lazy chunks by entry set, so each slice must be measured on the build routes and may need re-exports, as slice 3 did. (c) `new Worker(new URL('./physicsWorker.js', import.meta.url))` resolves against the bundle in the build and the module in the sources, so the client must keep that spelling or move with the worker file; the dist suite and a Barnes-Hut run in the build prove it. (d) `tools/build-irreversibility-audit.mjs` and the docs facts cite `js/physics.js` lines, so each slice runs `audit:irreversible` and `docs:sync`. (e) The wall-clock grace period is a model behavior: replacing it with simulation time is a scientific decision, not part of any slice, and is recorded here for Carl. (1) THE VERSION: `gravitas.artifact` stays at 1. The corpus row (`not-constrained-state`) says a 2.0.0 reader refuses a quantity whose uncertainty kind it does not know, in its own words, and drops `fit` and `correlatedWith` without a word; the second is acceptable because no reader needs either, and the first is safe because it is a capability-required refusal. So the writers keep their 2.0.0 output by default (`fitArtifact` gains an `extended` option and writes the new states and the record only when asked), and `legacyView()` gives a 2.0.0 reader the envelope it can open: each refused state becomes `none`, `fit` and `correlatedWith` are left out, a failed quantity (which has no value) is left out, and each loss is listed in the warnings as `extended:<id>:<kind>`. The way back is exact for the three 2.0.0 kinds and for them alone, which `tests/uncertaintyContract.test.js` holds on every kind and basis. Version 2 waits for Prompt 176. (2) THE STATES: `not-constrained` (the data leave the value open), `failed` (no result; `reason`, and a `null` value), `assumed` (taken as exact, which is not the unknown that `none` is), `model-limited` (a model error `floor` bounds the precision), `limit` (a nondetection: an `upper` or `lower` bound, with `level`). The asymmetric interval already existed as `lo` and `hi`; it gains a validated `level` on every kind that has one, and the sides are read from the value. The state names follow the compatibility fixtures of Prompt 134, not a new spelling. (3) THE FIT: the fit's result record (model and version, parameters by quantity id, the covariance in a stated order with each parameter's registry unit, the statistic and degrees of freedom, residual count and rms, the rows' digest, algorithm, settings and seed (null: the grid and the refinement are deterministic), convergence, rank) is built by `fitRecord` beside `fitArtifact`; no second representation was made. `js/inference/fit.js` gains `rankAt`: the information matrix is scaled to unit diagonal, its eigenvalues are read against the largest, and a parameter with at least 1% of its weight in a direction below 1e-8 of it, or one the model does not use, is not constrained. `infer.js` writes the result as `results.fit.rank`, flags the parameters, and warns `notConstrained`, in both languages; no fitted value and no sigma changed. The tolerance and the 1% are stated choices, not tuned to a case. (4) THE FORMULA: `evaluate` takes `assumed` (exact); `evaluateStates` in `js/formula/evidence.js` takes `model-limited` (its floor propagates) and one `limit`, and refuses `not-constrained`, `failed`, `interval` and a bare `limit` in words in both languages. A limit passes through a formula that rises or falls steadily from a quarter of it to the whole, checked at four points, not proved, with the other inputs exact: the result is a limit with the bound flipped if the formula falls. It lives beside the derivation record so the language stays under its byte ceiling (engine 5,932 of 6,144 gzipped; grader 6,374 of 6,656). (5) THE TEXT: `formatUncertain` writes a quantity at the precision its uncertainty sets (a sigma, or a symmetric interval's half-width; the smaller side of an asymmetric one; a limit as "<" or ">"; a model floor as the sigma) and says which method it used on request; `parseUncertain` reads a typed uncertainty ("±", "+/-", "9.81(2)", "+0.05 -0.03", "<", ">") through the shared number reader, handed in so the module stays a leaf. Both live in `js/platform/uncertain.js`, not in `js/format.js`, which is a source of the instructor bundle (a change to it needs the passphrase rebuild); nothing imports the new module yet, so no route pays for it until Prompt 151 adopts it. | D-R10-23 | Departure (1) of D-R10-13 repaired and departure (2) kept: a star that absorbs a planet, gas giant or asteroid conserves momentum the way the black-hole path does; rocky fragmentation stays as it is, recorded as a documented departure | `js/validation/engineTolerances.js` (36fb1d0c) | decision, taken by Carl and carried out here. **Repair (1):** `absorb_into_star` and `absorb_into_black_hole` (`js/engine/bodies.js`) are two callers of one `absorbInto`: the host takes the mass-weighted position and velocity (all four written only if finite), the spin term mu (r_rel x v_rel) goes to the same ledger (`bankAbsorbedSpin`; a star has no spin field, a hole keeps its `spin_angular_momentum`). Gating is the hole's: `mutual_gravity` on and `star_only_gravity` off, otherwise the star keeps its state and `bankDiscardedMomentum` records `m v`; a `model_owned` star also keeps its state (apply_step's own refusal: a prescribed model owns the motion), which the hole's gate never needed. The three star sites in `js/engine/collisions.js` collapse into one `starAbsorbs`. **Tolerance, committed first** (`36fb1d0c`, before any check using it existed or ran): `OUTCOMES.momentumScale` = 1e-12 of the sum of the magnitudes of m q over the two bodies (the scale is the sum of magnitudes because the net can be small), from six roundings of a mass-weighted merge (7e-16 at worst) with three orders of margin, and from the smallest effect it has to see: a Ceres-mass asteroid is 1e-10 of the scale, two orders above it. **Result:** the star's momentum error is 0 to display precision against 1e-12 for the planet (30 Earth masses), the gas giant (2 Jupiter masses) and the asteroid, and so is the hand-worked absolute total (M v_star + m v_body); the one validation check takes the larger of the two errors as a fraction of the sum of the magnitudes of m v, over 66 cases: a 4 solar-mass star at (1.5, -0.5), a 3.7 solar-mass star with non-round bodies and velocities, and a 60-case sweep from a fixed linear congruential sequence. The round-number cases measure exactly 0, so the margin is measured on the sweep: the largest round-off is 1.7e-16 of the scale (about 1.5 ulp) against 1e-12, 5.8e3 times under it; the comment in `engineTolerances.js` says so, the number is unchanged. Before, on the same three cases, the total after the event was short by 0.5734, 10.89 and 2.43e-6 (planet, giant, asteroid) of totals near 6.3e3, which is 1.7e-3 of the scale for the giant. The same check fails on the old engine (1.72e-3 against 1e-12; the group is 18 of 19 there) and passes on the new (19 of 19). The suite's check count stays 332 on purpose: it is printed in `js/i18n/en.js`, which the instructor bundle reads, so the group replaces the old departure check with this one and adds none. The centre of mass, the banked spin against mu (r_rel x v_rel) worked by hand, and the three non-participating cases (mutual gravity off, `star_only_gravity` on, a model-owned star), which keep their state and account for the discarded momentum, are pinned in `tests/engineConservation.test.js` instead, with the same hand-worked numbers as the hole's. **Goldens that moved, each from a star absorbing something:** `tests/fixtures/engineEventsGolden.json` white-dwarf-binary:3 (hash only: the first 'stellar-absorption' payload is v3's, and the first later event that differs is the one at 12.77 s, from a star that really moved) and supernova-remnant:3 (the first merge payload, of stars that had absorbed bodies before, in the eleventh figure; hash; events 0 to 31 are v3's bit for bit). The impact event reports the impact: `starAbsorbs` snapshots the star's position and velocity before the merge moves them (an earlier version of this change built the payload after the merge, which understated relativeSpeed by M/(M+m); `tests/engineConservation.test.js` now pins relativeSpeed, position and masses against the hand-worked impact); `tests/fixtures/engineConservationGolden.json` stellar-graveyard:5 and compact-object-zoo:3 (mutual gravity on: totals, drift, energies, histories and the spin ledger, which now includes the stars'; the hand-pinned `spin` at sample 1 of the graveyard moves from -0.000393366119608 to -0.000303633314114), black-hole-billiards:3 and hungry-hungry-holes:3 (one-way gravity: only the discarded-momentum ledger gains the stars' terms). Unchanged: neutron-star-collision:3, hungry-hungry-holes:3 events, binary-bh:4:RK4 and galactic-collision:1, which have no star absorption, and the world golden (`tests/scenarioGeometry.test.js`), which compares initial builds; no lesson stage or scenario build has a star absorbing something (the lesson scene audit and the full Jest run are unchanged by it). **Kept (2):** a rocky collision above relative speed 15 still multiplies each body's mass by 0.9 and throws floor(speed/8)+2 fragments of tiny fixed mass, so a tenth of the pair's mass leaves; the check that measures it stays, now labelled kept by decision, and "What is not validated" (`tools/validation-gaps.json`, PHYSICS_VALIDATION.md, the model page) lists it with its measured size and no longer lists the star departure. **Size:** three sources ceilings rose by exactly the measured overrun, rounded up to 0.1 KB, under the standing approval of 2026-10-10: front-door 2115.5 to 2116.8, sandbox 2115.5 to 2116.8, figure 2389 to 2390.3 (re-measured after merging v3 at 17d89876); no request or line ceiling moved (`bodies.js` 1428 to 1477 lines, `collisions.js` 1388 to 1379, both under 1,500, and no module is at a listed ceiling). | **DELEGATED** | Carl, 2026-10-20, in chat, go with the recommendation (repair the star path, keep rocky fragmentation and record it); the tolerance, the regenerated goldens and the spin ledger now holding the stars' share are not yet reviewed by Carl | Returning the star to `star.mass += body.mass` (the committed momentum checks fail); widening `momentumScale` to pass (refused); a hole or star that should keep its state when it absorbs (a new gate, not a change to this one); repairing rocky fragmentation (its own model decision) | 137 |
